24.18.0.en: Father Serapion: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked [19].

24.18.1.en: For there shall be no reward to the evil man.

24.19.0.en: The candle of the wicked shall be put out [20].

24.19.1.en: He repeated the same commandment as in verse 1 and in Proverbs 23:17, because God knows how hard it is for man to accept it, although he realizes how great its blessings are for him and how God is pleased with its fulfillment.

24.19.2.en: It is not fitting for us to envy the wicked for their circumstances, for time quickly passes and the wicked stand in judgment, their lamps having been put out, and their destiny is outer darkness. They have no share in the eternal inheritance and no place in the bosom of God...

24.19.3.en: By the putting out of the lamp of the wicked is meant the destruction of their children, for what they gather of the wealth of injustice and store up for their offspring is quickly scattered, and their offspring lose the divine blessing, if they walk in the evil way of their fathers. But the righteous man leaves blessing as an inheritance to his children according to the flesh as well as according to the Spirit, if they walk in the holy way of their father.

24.19.4.en: Here we notice God's wonderful regard for man. God offers man, however great his evils, opportunities and possibilities that he might shine like a star in the midst of heaven; but the wicked rejects the divine light by his evil will, and so every trace of light in him is put out.

24.19.5.en: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king.

24.20.0.en: Meddle not with them that are given to change [21].

24.20.1.en: Truly, the fear of the Lord and submission to Him are followed by submission, in the Lord, to those in authority.

24.20.2.en: The man of God does not meddle with those given to change, that is, he does not take part with those who rise in rebellion, nor cooperate with the schemers, who find their pleasure in revolts and intrigues against civil or church leaders.

24.20.3.en: * "My son, fear thou the LORD and the king," that is, fear Christ the true God, and the king, or Solomon means by the king one who rules himself before ruling others. "Be not disobedient to either of them." Truly, whoever does not honor the king chosen by God insults God.

24.21.0.en: St. John Chrysostom: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both? [22].

24.21.1.en: Whoever acquires the fear of the Lord within him, along with the boldness he gains before God, and his freedom from fear of men however high their positions, and even from fear of death, nevertheless in a spirit of deep humility fears God and seeks His pleasure and approval, and he respects those of social standing, not in servility and humiliation, but in a spirit of contentment and in order to live a life full of peace. He does not meddle with those given to change, that is, those without fixed principles, who incline toward intrigues and revolts.

24.21.2.en: It is regrettable that even within the Church there are those who love biting criticism and resisting every church arrangement and order; they gather for themselves the wrath of God, and calamities await them.

24.21.3.en: The man who rebels against God and the leaders reaps for himself an inner rebellion; his body rebels against his spirit, and his emotions rebel against his mind, so that he carries within him bitter calamities. And while he thinks that he is seeking to reform society and the Church, he finds himself dissolute, and loses his harmony even with himself.

24.22.0.en: 23 These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. 24 He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him: 25 But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them. 26 Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.

24.22.1.en: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment [23].

24.22.2.en: By saying "These things also belong to the wise" he reveals that he recorded what precedes as one unit, which began by asking for the fear of the Lord and ended with the obligation of the fear of the Lord and obedience to the leaders. And what appears in the rest of this chapter is considered something like an appendix dealing with four important matters in the life of the believer, namely: no partiality, counting the cost, abstaining from false witness, and not being slothful. Perhaps these are considered an introduction to the next collection of proverbs.

24.22.3.en: He warns us against respect of persons, for whoever fears God does not fear men, and shows partiality to no one because of kinship in the flesh, or wealth, or honor, or one in authority. For in true humility he seeks the truth and proclaims it.

24.22.4.en: It befits rulers and civil leaders, as well as spiritual ones, to hold to this principle, as it befits every believer to hold to it, even if he does not have a leadership position in the eyes of society.

24.22.5.en: In the story of Susanna, which is in the addition to Daniel, there is a wonderful picture of the young Daniel, who boldly did not fear the two elders who had led astray all those around them; and courageously he rescued Susanna, who was falsely accused, and exposed the two elders for their corruption.

24.22.6.en: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse.

24.23.1.en: Because of fear of the wicked, some flatter him and justify his actions, and even regard him as righteous. But when the truth is uncovered, people shun this deceiver at the expense of the truth, and the person brings a curse upon his own head.

24.23.2.en: Many contemporary societies have been struck by this blow, justifying the errors of some wicked people, and sometimes even praising them as though they were good and heroic deeds.

24.23.3.en: Perhaps the address here is to leaders and men of the judiciary, who for one reason or another justify the errors of some criminals at the expense of the poor and wronged classes.

24.24.0.en: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them [25].

24.24.1.en: In contrast to those who show partiality to the wicked and call them good, we find others who discipline the wicked, whether by rebuke or by corporal punishment; these the people will surely respect when everyone confirms the corruption of the wicked, and how the judges or rulers restrained them from practicing their evils, so blessings come upon them.

24.24.2.en: * "But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them" (Prov 24:25).

24.24.3.en: I choose that the Lord visit my sins and correct my offenses here in this world, so that Abraham may say to me there what he said about poor Lazarus in his conversation with the rich man: "Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented" (Lk 16:25). For this reason, when the Lord rebukes and disciplines us, we must not be ungrateful. Let us then understand that our rebuke in the present time is so that we may receive consolation in the future. As the Apostle says: "But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world" (1 Cor 11:32). For this reason Job also accepted all his sufferings willingly, saying: "What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?" (Job 2:10).

24.25.0.en: Origen: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer [26].

24.25.1.en: He who gives upright judgments without partiality is honored and trusted, and is the object of the admiration and love of many. The kissing of the lips here refers to respect through love, not fear, and the kiss in the East is still known in this sense. As it is said in the Psalm: "Kiss the Son, lest he be angry" (Ps 2:12).

24.25.2.en: The kiss is also used as an acknowledgment of a person's justice and wisdom, and of trust in him and submission to him. Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Thou shalt be over my house, and at thy mouth shall all my people kiss" (Gen 41:40).

24.26.0.en: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field;

24.26.2.en: The wise man calls us to count the cost, so that we build the house only after preparing the work: we choose the suitable site for the house, choose the kind and size of the buildings, calculate their cost, and see whether we are able to complete the work. As the Lord Christ Himself says: "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish" (Lk 14:28-30).

24.26.3.en: The Old Testament gives us an example of those who began to build the tower of Babel so that its top might reach to heaven, carrying obstinacy and resistance against God; since they did not count the cost, they did not finish the work (Gen 11:9).

24.26.4.en: * Scripture says: "Prepare thy work for thy departure, and make it ready in thy field." Now I think that "thy departure" means our going out from this world and leaving it. "What man is he that liveth, and shall not see death? shall he deliver his soul from the hand of the grave?" (Ps 89:48). For man's nature was condemned in Adam and fell into corruption, because in folly he disobeyed the commandment given to him.

24.26.5.en: St. Cyril the Great: * Whoever values the safety of his soul takes care not to be in danger, by keeping his freedom from sin, so that he may preserve for himself the benefit of his former good works.

24.26.6.en: The Canons of the Apostles: * Let us count the cost of the spiritual tower of towering height, and examine it deeply and carefully beforehand... Let us take into consideration first the faults plainly, and dig and remove the corruption and the refuse of the passions, so that we may lay the strong foundations of simplicity and humility upon the solid ground of our living breast, or rather the foundations are laid upon the rock of the Gospel (Lk 6:48); thus the tower of spiritual virtues rises, and is able to stand and to rise to the heights of heaven in complete safety and without being shaken.

24.26.7.en: Father Isaac: * It is a day of shouting and trumpet (Zeph 1:16). It is a day of grief and sighing for those who have not prepared their works well for the road, that is, for their departure from the body to meet God profitably.

24.27.0.en: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips [28].

24.27.1.en: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me:

24.28.0.en: I will render to the man according to his work [29].

24.28.1.en: Returning evil for evil, or revenge, strips man of the life of purity and corrupts holiness, especially if he gives false testimony against his brother with the intention of taking revenge on him, even if this brother had previously testified falsely against him. For evil is not resisted with evil. A man's truthfulness and the holiness of his life are things that must not be touched, whatever the motive. The Apostle says: "Recompense to no man evil for evil" (Rom 12:17).

24.28.2.en: When the believer realizes that God embraces him, upholds him, solves his problems, and defends him, he does not avenge himself, but leans on God's breast. The Apostle commands us: "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord" (Rom 12:19).

24.28.3.en: The man of God desires to see those who trouble him turn back from the evil they practice and be sanctified. This he cannot attain by avenging himself, but by leaving the matter in the hands of God, who is able to renew the heart and sanctify the soul.

24.28.4.en: * The utmost desire of the injured man is to see vengeance; this God accomplishes for him in its fullest measure on condition that he does not try to avenge himself. Leave it to God to follow up the injuries that have befallen you.

24.29.0.en: 30 I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding; 31 And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down. 32 Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction. 33 Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: 34 So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

24.29.1.en: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding [30].

24.29.2.en: The wise man called us to a life of continual striving by saying: "Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days" (Eccl 11:1). For our faith in the Lord grants us springs of water of His Holy Spirit flowing from our bellies (Jn 7:38); we enjoy His divine help, and feed on Him as the bread of life if we cast out works of love toward God and toward our neighbor, and He returns it to us as surpassing heavenly love.

24.29.3.en: Origen sees that a man does not enjoy the light of knowledge while in slackness and sloth, but enjoys wisdom and knowledge through practice and diligence.

24.29.4.en: * Do not think that wisdom comes before its being enacted in works, but works must come first, and wisdom be sought afterward... He says: "Sow to yourselves in righteousness" (Hos 10:12)... and after that you can do what follows: "enlighten yourselves with the light of knowledge."

24.30.0.en: Origen: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down [31].

24.30.1.en: Then I saw, and considered it well.

24.31.0.en: I looked upon it, and received instruction [32].

24.31.1.en: The wise man has previously warned us against sloth (Prov 6:10-11; 20:4). Here he presents a precise picture of the field and vineyard of the slothful man, and one's soul grieves for the owner of the field and the vineyard, for the ruin, drought, thorns, and thistles that befall them only reveal the destruction and ruin that has befallen the heart of their owner.

24.31.2.en: The nettle is a kind of thorn that abounds in abandoned regions (Isa 34:13; Hos 9:6). And the bramble is the thorn tree.

24.31.3.en: And even if a man has no need of money, sloth corrupts his inner life, shatters his personality, and removes from him the taste of life, so that it becomes tasteless and aimless.

24.32.0.en: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep [33].

24.33.0.en: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man! [34].

24.33.1.en: When the time of work comes, the slothful man sleeps, and thinks there is rest and happiness in this, but he is surprised by poverty running swiftly to fall upon his possessions as well as upon his mind and heart, so that his inner energies are shattered, and want invades him like an armed man who takes him captive.

24.33.2.en: May I possess You, O Wisdom of God!

24.33.3.en: * In You, O Wisdom of God, my whole life is built; upon You my soul is established as a holy building; I truly become a temple in which Your Holy Spirit dwells.

24.33.4.en: He fills it with treasures of wisdom, learning, and knowledge. * According to Your promise You become a wall of fire surrounding my whole being.

24.33.5.en: So the fiery darts of the enemy cannot pass through to me.

24.33.6.en: You are the fortress of my life, You and the One who works in me; I bear Your righteousness, and I am fortified by Your grace.

24.33.7.en: * In You I become like a tree planted by the rivers of water, bearing much fruit, whose leaf does not wither.

24.33.8.en: The wicked are deprived of union with You, so they become like chaff in the wind; they take pride in their abilities, capacities, and strength, and plan to destroy the wise.

24.33.9.en: But soon they perish, and the righteous wise are saved.

24.33.10.en: In You I grow constantly; time cannot break my depths, nor sickness corrupt my strength, nor events take from me the spirit of wisdom and the treasures of learning and knowledge.

24.33.11.en: In You I go from victory to victory.

24.33.12.en: And I experience the glory of salvation day by day.

24.33.13.en: I enter the battles of the devil fortified in You!

24.33.14.en: * I stand before the court in silence.

24.33.15.en: What shall I answer? And how shall I defend myself?

24.33.16.en: I confess that I deserve eternal death!

24.33.17.en: But You came forward on my behalf.

24.33.18.en: And You, the Judge and the Holy One, were silent and did not open Your mouth!

24.33.19.en: You were silent, O holy Word of God, that in You I may speak, and in You be justified, and in You claim the right to enter the heavenly glories.

24.33.20.en: You did not open Your mouth at Your trial, that You might open for me the door of Paradise which I closed by my sins.

24.33.21.en: * By Your silence You granted me the power of the word, You granted me wisdom as an eternal light that death cannot extinguish.

24.33.22.en: If distress comes upon me, however severe, my strength will not fail, for You are my strength!

24.33.23.en: The distress that crushes the fool proves me and bears witness to Your grace working in me.

24.33.24.en: * May I possess You, so that my heart is widened with love, and I love everyone, even those who oppose me, for You loved me while I was an enemy, and reconciled me with the Father by Your precious Blood.

24.33.25.en: Grant me to return love for love, so that I do not cease to support every afflicted person, whatever his nationality, religion, or conduct.

24.33.26.en: May I love everyone for Your sake, O Lover of all mankind!

24.33.27.en: * May I possess You, O Desire of the nations, whose mouth is most sweet, and who is altogether lovely.

24.33.28.en: You are the sweetness of my soul.

24.33.30.en: Without You I have no life.

24.33.31.en: You are my hope, You are the Physician of my soul!

24.33.32.en: You change me from corruption to incorruption.

24.33.33.en: You raise me from the death of sin that I may enjoy the experience of the power of Your resurrection and its joy.

24.33.34.en: When all shut their doors before me, I find Your opened side waiting for me, and Your divine embrace welcoming me.

24.33.35.en: And Your heavens await my coming!

24.33.36.en: * Grant me love toward all mankind, so that my heart does not rejoice at the fall of an enemy of mine among men, for I have no real enemy but the devil himself.

24.33.37.en: As for men, they are all my brothers.

24.33.38.en: Gladden my heart with their salvation and success.

24.33.39.en: * Remove evil from the wicked, so that their lamp is not put out.

24.33.40.en: Sanctify their lives, so that they seek not what belongs to the world, but what belongs to Your eternal Kingdom.

24.33.41.en: * Grant me the spirit of the fear of the Lord and godliness.

24.33.42.en: That I may not fear any man, and in a spirit of humility not take part in rebellion or biting criticism!

24.33.43.en: But let me not praise a wicked man for his wickedness, nor show partiality because of kinship or profit.

24.33.44.en: * Receive the building of my inner house, for no human hand can establish it, but Your divine wisdom lays its foundations and raises it up.

24.33.45.en: It rises even to heaven, and enjoys Your dwelling in it!

24.33.46.en: * Work, O Wisdom of God, in me, and work even in those who oppose me.

24.33.47.en: For what I desire is the salvation of all!

24.33.48.en: * Grant me Your fiery Spirit who is ever at work, so that I do not slacken or grow careless, nor seek sleep and sloth!

24.33.49.en: But in You let me become a burning spiritual coal!
